messages:
Rae (People Ops): Quick thread  we're seeing recurring requests for a "satellite hub" schedule where teammates work one week per month in a different state— need alignment on stipend, payroll, and a short attestation template. Thoughts?

Owen (Eng): I'm planning to be in Seattle 1 week/month starting July to pair with infra. Do I keep full monthly WFH stipend or is it prorated? Also do I have to change my homebase?

Mina (Finance): Short version: homebase only changes if you intend to be physically located >90 consecutive days. For stipend, our default is prorate by calendar days at homebase vs away for recurring patterns to reduce withholding complexity.

Hector (Legal): Caveat: repeating work in another state can create employer nexus risk, especially if the role includes hiring, sales, or contracting. Even purely internal work can raise payroll withholding questions. Please flag any candidate interviews or vendor negotiations.

Rae (People Ops): Proposed interim rule everyone agrees on: default = calendar-day proration; exceptions allowed with manager + Finance signoff for business justification (e.g., company-paid dedicated desk). We'll add a short attestation for employees to confirm they won't do recruiting/contracting while at the hub unless pre-approved.

Owen (Eng): Example math? If I spend 7 days in Seattle out of 31 days in July and stipend is $200, what do I get?

Mina (Finance): Payout = (homebase_days / total_days_in_month) * stipend. If homebase_days=24, payout = (24/31)*200 = $154.84 -> we round to nearest dollar, so $155. Any state withholding notes will appear on the paystub.

Rae (People Ops): Employee process we'll use: 1) open a People Ops case with pattern and hub address, 2) indicate if you'll do interviews, contract work, or vendor negotiations while there, 3) choose reimbursement vs stipend, 4) request IT shipping if needed. Target response within 3 business days.

PeopleOps-Bot: New case created: #43301 "Owen - Seattle 1wk/mo". Rae will triage.

Owen (Eng): If the company pays the coworking invoice directly, does that affect payout?

Mina (Finance): Yes  if Redwood pays vendor directly (invoiced), we treat it as a company-covered expense and the employee won't receive the stipend for that period. That avoids duplication and usually is non-taxable to the employee.

Hector (Legal): Also note: if you plan to interview or sign up contractors locally while at a hub, you must get pre-approval. That activity materially increases nexus risk. We'll include a short checkbox attestation in the case response.

Owen (Eng): About IT shipping: can my laptop be shipped to the hub address? Any customs concerns if it's near-border?

Rae (People Ops): IT will ship after People Ops approves the case and an IT ticket is opened. For international hubs we'll require return plan and may ask for temporary import documentation. For domestic hubs it's straightforward.

Mina (Finance): Payroll request timing: submit your case at least 10 business days before payroll cutoff so we can compute proration and any state withholding adjustments. Late submissions may cause retroactive payroll corrections.

Rae (People Ops): We'll draft a one-pager "satellite hub FAQ" and a short attestation template for recurring patterns (no recruiting/contracting without pre-approval). I'll post the draft here and link the doc. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
